Trademark Details |url=https://trademarks.justia.com/880/56/block-88056283.html |website=Justia Trademarks |publisher=Justia Trademarks |access-date=19 April 2023}} and also known by his initials '''JJJ''', is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]]. Jackson was selected by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] with the fourth overall pick of the [[2018 NBA draft]]. In 2023, he was named to his first [[NBA All-Star]] team, later winning [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award|Defensive Player of the Year]] that same season. Jackson is renowned for his defensive dominance, particularly his exceptional rim protection; he [[List of NBA annual blocks leaders|led the league in blocks per game]] for two consecutive seasons in 2021–22 and 2022–23. ==Early life== Jaren Walter Jackson Jr. was born on September 15, 1999, in [[Plainfield, New Jersey]]. Jaren started his high school career with [[Park Tudor School]] in [[Indianapolis]]. He played varsity for three years, where he averaged 10 points, 6 rebounds and 3 blocks per game.{{Cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/jaren-jackson/543Mzlz0EeOzMAAmVebBJg/gendersport/basketball-stats.htm|title=Jaren Jackson's High School Basketball Stats|website=MaxPreps.com|language=en-US|access-date=January 18, 2017}} Jackson won two [[Indiana High School Athletic Association|IHSAA]] state basketball championships while at Park Tudor.{{cite web |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle |date=March 28, 2015 |title=Class 2A: Park Tudor wins 4th title in 5 years |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/03/28/class-park-tudor-repeats-win-frankton/70597226 |access-date=September 7, 2023 |website=Indystar.com |publisher=Indy Star}} He was teammates with future [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier University]] standout and future professional basketball player [[Trevon Bluiett]].{{cite web|title=Park Tudor: 84 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171231051616/http://wishtv.com/2014/03/29/park-tudor-84-westview-57/|url-status=dead}} He then transferred to [[La Lumiere School]] in [[La Porte, Indiana]] for his senior year,{{Cite web|url=http://www.verbalcommits.com/players/jaren-jackson-jr|title=Verbal Commits {{!}} Jaren Jackson, Jr. Player Profile, Highlights, Offers, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202070717/http://www.verbalcommits.com/players/jaren-jackson-jr|url-status=dead}} where he met [[Jordan Poole]]{{Cite web |last=Cole |first=Damichael |date=May 9, 2022 |title=Jordan Poole and Jaren Jackson Jr. on being high school roommates, NBA playoffs rivals |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2022/05/09/jaren-jackson-jr-jordan-poole-high-school-roommates-nba-playoffs/9661973002 |access-date=September 7, 2023 |website=indystar.com |via=[[Memphis Commercial Appeal]]}} and started for their varsity squad. ===Recruiting=== [[File:20170329 MCDAAG Jaren Jackson Jr. dunks in front of Nicholas Richards.jpg|thumb|Jackson dunking the ball, 2017]] Jackson was appraised for being one of the top players in the 2017 graduating class.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/jaren-jackson-jr|title=Jaren Jackson Jr. {{!}} NBADraft.net|website=Nbadraft.net|language=en|access-date=January 18, 2017}} [[Scout.com]] ranked Jackson the fifth-best player nationally,{{Cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/player/193446-jaren-jackson|title=Jaren Jackson, La Lumiere School PF - Scout|website=Scout.com|language=en|access-date=January 18, 2017}} first at his position and second overall in the [[Midwestern United States|Midwest]] region. [[247Sports]] ranked him 7th nationally,{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Jaren-Jackson-78413|title=Jaren Jackson, La Lumiere School, Power Forward|website=247Sports|access-date=January 18, 2017}} being 4th in his position. [[ESPN]] ranked him 8th in the ESPN 100,{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/207895|title=Jaren Jackson - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=January 18, 2017}} being 2nd in his position and 2nd regionally. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}}{{College athlete recruit entry|40=|247 stars=5|feet=6|highschool=[[La Lumiere School]] [[Park Tudor School]]|hometown=[[Carmel, IN]]|inches=10|position=PF|recruit=Jaren Jackson Jr.|weight=226|commitdate=September 15, 2016|espn grade=93|rivals stars=5|scout stars=5}}{{College athlete recruit end|247 overall=7|rivals overall=6|espn overall=8}} Jackson was recruited by a number of notable programs, including Michigan State, [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]], [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], and several more.{{Cite news |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle |date=July 3, 2016 |title=Jaren Jackson Jr. helps USA U17 team to gold |language=en |newspaper=Indianapolis Star |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/07/03/jaren-jackson-jr-helps-usa-u17-team-gold/86659816 |access-date=September 7, 2023}} He was invited to partake in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] played on March 29, 2017.{{Cite news|url=https://www.landof10.com/michigan-state/michigan-state-jaren-jackson-jr-brian-bowen-mcdonalds-all-american|title=Michigan State signee Jaren Jackson Jr. reacts to McDonald's selection|date=January 22, 2017|newspaper=Land of 10|language=en-US|access-date=January 23, 2017}} ==College career== On September 15, 2016, Jaren Jackson Jr. announced his intentions to play for [[Tom Izzo]] at [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]]. He signed the [[letter of intent]] on November 9, 2016. Jackson made his collegiate debut on November 10, 2017, recording 13 points and a season-high 13 rebounds in a blowout 98–66 win over [[North Florida Ospreys men's basketball|North Florida]]. Four days later, he recorded a then-season-high 19 points in an 88–81 loss to #1-ranked [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]]. On December 5, Jackson put up 11 points and a career-high 8 blocks in a 62–52 win over [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]]. Four days later, he recorded 17 points and another career-high 13 rebounds in a blowout 88–63 win over [[Southern Utah Thunderbirds men's basketball|Southern Utah]]. On January 22, 2018, Jackson recorded a then-season-high 21 points to go with 11 rebounds and 6 blocks in an 87–74 win over [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]]. On February 13, he put up a career-high 27 points in a blowout 87–57 win over [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]]. At the end of the regular season for Michigan State, he was named both the Big Ten's Defensive Player of the Year, Freshman of the Year, Big Ten's All-Freshman Team, and the [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]]'s third team. On April 2, Jackson declared his entry into the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he was considered a potential top-tier lottery selection. ==Professional career== ===Memphis Grizzlies (2018–2026)=== ==== 2018–2021: Early years ==== On June 21, 2018, Jackson was selected with the fourth overall pick by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{Cite web | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2774199-jaren-jackson-picked-by-grizzlies-no-4-in-nba-draft-twitter-loves-upside |title = Jaren Jackson Picked by Grizzlies No. 4 in NBA Draft; Twitter Loves Upside|website=Bleacherreport.com}} On July 1, 2018, he signed a multi-year, rookie-scale contract with the Grizzlies.{{cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Jaren Jackson Jr. to multi-year contract |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-jaren-jackson-jr-to-multi-year-contract-180701 |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 2, 2018 |date=July 1, 2018}} On March 29, 2019, Jackson was shut down for the remainder of the season due to a deep bruise to his right thigh.{{Cite web | url=https://twitter.com/mgiannotto/status/1111663747066675202 | title=Memphis Grizzlies coach JB Bickerstaff just confirmed that Jaren Jackson Jr. and Kyle Anderson won't play the rest of this season|website=Twitter.com}} On December 13, 2019, Jackson scored a career-high 43 points, including 9 three-pointers (which tied a franchise record set by [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]] in 2007) in a 127–114 loss to the [[2019–20 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/grizzlies/news/jaren-jackson-jr-historic-night-in-loss-to-bucks|title=Jaren Jackson Jr.'s Historic Night Was Not Enough For The Memphis Grizzlies To Overcome The Milwaukee Bucks|first=Anthony|last=Sain|website=Si.com|access-date=February 3, 2022}} On January 30, 2020, Jackson was suspended for one game without pay for leaving the bench during an altercation between the Grizzlies and the [[2019–20 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]].{{Cite web|title=Knicks' Payton, Grizzlies' Guduric and Jackson Jr. suspended; Knicks' Morris Sr. and Grizzlies' Crowder fined|url=https://pr.nba.com/new-yorks-payton-memphis-guduric-and-jackson-jr-suspended-new-yorks-morris-sr-and-memphis-crowder-fined/|access-date=October 11, 2021|website=NBA|date=January 31, 2020 }} On January 28, Jackson recorded a career-high 7 blocks in a 104–96 win over the [[2019–20 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202001280MEM.html|title=Denver Nuggets at Memphis Grizzlies Box Score, January 28, 2020|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 3, 2022}} On August 4, 2020, Jackson suffered a torn meniscus in his left knee in a 99–109 loss to the [[2019–20 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]] hosted in the [[2020 NBA Bubble|Bubble]] and was expected to miss the remainder of the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]].{{cite web|title=Jaren Jackson Jr. medical update|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/jaren-jackson-jr-medical-update-200804|date=August 4, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 4, 2020}} On December 16, 2020, the Grizzlies announced that they had exercised the team option on Jackson.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies exercise 2021-22 contract options on Ja Morant, Jaren Jackson Jr., Brandon Clarke and Grayson Allen|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-exercise-2021-22-contract-options-on-ja-morant-jaren-jackson-jr-brandon-clarke-and-grayson-allen-201216|date=December 16, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 16, 2020}} On April 21, 2021, Jackson made his return, putting up 15 points, 8 rebounds, and 4 blocks in a loss to the [[2020–21 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31307393|title=Memphis Grizzlies' Jaren Jackson Jr. says returning to court after injury 'a big win'|website=ESPN.com|last=Youngmisuk|first=Ohm|date=April 21, 2021|access-date=April 22, 2021}} Two days later, Jackson scored a season-high 23 points in a 130–128 win over the [[2020–21 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202104230POR.html|title=Memphis Grizzlies at Portland Trail Blazers Box Score, April 23, 2021|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 3, 2022}} After a series of play-in tournament wins, the Grizzlies qualified for the playoffs for the first time since [[2017 NBA playoffs|2017]]. They faced the top-seeded [[Utah Jazz]] during their first round series. On May 31, Jackson scored a postseason career-high 21 points in a 120–113 Game 4 loss.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401327908|title=Jazz vs. Grizzlies - Game Recap - May 31, 2021 |website=ESPN.com|access-date=February 3, 2022}} The Grizzlies would eventually lose the series in five games. ==== 2021–2023: Defensive Player of the Year and All-Star selection ==== On October 18, 2021, Jackson signed a four-year, $105 million extension with the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/report-grizzlies-jaren-jackson-jr-agree-to-105m-extension|website=NBA.com|title=Grizzlies, Jaren Jackson Jr. agree to reported $105M extension|date=October 19, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On January 9, 2022, Jackson scored 21 points and tied a career-high with 12 rebounds in a 127–119 win over the [[2021–22 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/postgame/lal-220109|title=Postgame Report: Grizzlies get franchise record ninth consecutive win with victory over Lakers|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 3, 2022}} On April 16, during Game 1 of the first round of the playoffs, Jackson logged 12 points and seven blocks in a 130–117 loss to the [[2021–22 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]]. His seven blocks set a Grizzlies franchise record for most blocks in a playoff game, surpassing [[Marc Gasol]]'s 6 on May 13, 2013.{{Cite web |title=Timberwolves stun Grizzlies, grab Game 1 with 130-117 win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/timberwolves-stun-grizzlies-grab-game-1-with-130-117-win/ |access-date=April 16, 2022 |website=CBS Sports}} The Grizzlies eventually defeated the Timberwolves in six games, with Jackson recording 18 points, 14 rebounds and two blocks in a 114–106 Game 6 win.{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Dave |date=April 30, 2022 |title=GRIZZLIES RALLY AGAIN PAST WOLVES 114-106 TO REACH 2ND ROUND |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100156 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} During the Grizzlies' second-round series, they faced the [[2021–22 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]]. On May 1, Jackson scored a playoff career-high 33 points, alongside ten rebounds, in a 117–116 Game 1 loss.{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Teresa M. |date=May 2, 2022 |title=WARRIORS RALLY AFTER GREEN EJECTED, BEAT GRIZZLIES IN GAME 1 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100231 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} The Grizzlies wound up losing the series in six games to the Warriors, who went on to win the [[NBA Finals]]. Jackson finished the [[2021–22 NBA season|2021–22 season]] leading the NBA in blocks per game at 2.3 and finished with the most blocks that season with 177 blocks, 40 more than the second-place finisher.{{Cite web |title=2021-22 NBA Player Stats: Totals |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2022_totals.html |access-date=2022-05-27 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} For his efforts, he was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive First Team]]{{Cite web |date=May 20, 2022 |title=Jaren Jackson Jr. named to Kia NBA All-Defensive First Team |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/jaren-jackson-jr-named-to-kia-nba-all-defensive-first-team-220520 |access-date=May 27, 2022 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} and finished fifth in Defensive Player of the Year voting.{{Cite web |title=Boston's Marcus Smart wins 2021-22 Kia Defensive Player of the Year award |url=https://www.nba.com/news/bostons-marcus-smart-wins-2021-22-kia-defensive-player-of-the-year-award |access-date=2022-05-27 |website=nba.com |language=en}} On June 30, 2022, Jackson underwent surgery to repair a stress fracture in his right foot and was ruled out for four-to-six months.{{Cite web |date=June 30, 2022 |title=Grizzlies' Jaren Jackson Jr. undergoes foot surgery, sidelined 4-6 months |url=https://www.nba.com/news/grizzlies-jaren-jackson-jr-undergoes-foot-surgery-sidelined-4-6-months |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} After missing the first 14 games of the 2022–23 season, he made his season debut on November 15, recording seven points, six rebounds and five blocks in a 113–102 loss to the [[2022–23 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web |date=November 16, 2022 |title=MCCOLLUM, PELICANS BEAT GRIZZLIES WITHOUT INJURED WILLIAMSON |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200206 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On December 12, Jackson recorded a career-high eight blocks, alongside 15 points, seven rebounds and two assists, in a 128–103 win over the [[2022–23 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Clay |date=December 12, 2022 |title=JONES, BROOKS POWER MEMPHIS TO 128-103 WIN OVER ATLANTA |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200404 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On January 5, 2023, he scored a season-high 31 points, alongside ten rebounds and three blocks, in a 123–115 win over the [[2022–23 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]].{{Cite web |last=Scanlon |first=Dick |date=January 5, 2023 |title=MORANT, JACKSON LEAD GRIZZLIES OVER MAGIC FOR 5TH STRAIGHT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200576 |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On February 2, Jackson was selected to his first [[NBA All-Star Game]] as a reserve forward for the Western Conference.{{Cite web |date=February 3, 2023 |title=2023 NBA All-Star reserves revealed |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-all-star-reserves-announced |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On April 5, Jackson scored a season-high 40 points, along with nine rebounds, three assists and four blocks in a 138–131 overtime loss against the New Orleans Pelicans.{{Cite web |last=Martel |first=Brett |date=April 6, 2023 |title=PELICANS TOP GRIZZLIES 138-131 IN OT, EARN PLAY-IN SPOT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/mem-vs-nop-0022201194 |access-date=April 10, 2023 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On 9 April, Jackson finished the regular season as the league leader in blocks for the second year in a row, averaging a career-high 3 blocks per game.{{cite web|title=Defensive Player Ladder: Brook Lopez ends season at No. 1|url=https://www.nba.com/news/defensive-player-ladder-april-2023-edition|date=April 11, 2023|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 11, 2023}} On April 16, in the opening game of the playoffs Jackson scored a game-high 31 points on 13-of-21 shooting from the field in a 128–112 loss against the [[2022–23 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |title=Hachimura's big 2nd half leads LA past Memphis in Game 1 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401540756 |access-date=April 16, 2023 |website=ESPN.com|date=April 16, 2023}} Memphis lost the series in six games.{{Cite web |date=2023-04-28 |title=Lakers obliterate Grizzlies 125-85, advance to 2nd round |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401541232 |access-date=2023-04-30 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} During the playoffs, Jackson was named for the first time the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award|Defensive Player of the Year]], and was named for the second consecutive time to the NBA All-Defensive First team.{{Cite web |title=Jaren Jackson Jr. named 2022-23 Kia NBA Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.nba.com/news/jaren-jackson-defensive-player-of-year |access-date=2023-04-30 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=May 10, 2023 |title=Jaren Jackson Jr. headlines 2022-23 Kia NBA All-Defensive teams |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2022-23-all-defensive-teams-announced |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} ==== 2023–2026: Second All-Star selection ==== Jackson Jr. started all 66 of his appearances for the Grizzlies during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 22.5 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jaren Jackson Jr. 2023–24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4277961/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On January 30, 2025, Jackson Jr. was named as reserve for the [[2025 NBA All-Star Game]], his second selection.{{cite web| title= Victor Wembanyama, Jaylen Brown highlight 2025 All-Star Game reserves | website=NBA.com | date=January 30, 2025 | url= https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-all-star-game-reserves | access-date=February 2, 2025}} He started all 77 of his appearances for Memphis in the [[2024–25 NBA season]], posting averages of 22.2 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 2.0 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jaren Jackson Jr. 2024–25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4277961/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On June 30, 2025, Jackson Jr. agreed to a five‑year, $240 million contract extension with the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45619864/sources-grizzlies-extend-jaren-jackson-jr-240m-deal|title=Sources: Grizzlies extend Jackson Jr. on $240M deal|publisher=ESPN|date=June 30, 2025}} On July 2, it was announced that Jackson would miss 10-to-12 weeks after undergoing surgery to repair a [[metatarsophalangeal joint sprain|turf toe injury]].{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies' Jaren Jackson Jr. has surgery for turf toe injury|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45646868/grizzlies-jaren-jackson-jr-surgery-turf-toe-injury|access-date=October 23, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} He went on to make 45 starts for the Grizzlies during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 19.8 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 1.9 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jaren Jackson Jr. 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4277961/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} === Utah Jazz (2026–present) === On February 3, 2026, Jackson Jr., [[John Konchar]], [[Jock Landale]], and [[Vince Williams Jr.]] were traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Kyle Anderson (basketball)|Kyle Anderson]], [[Walter Clayton Jr.]], [[Taylor Hendricks]], [[Georges Niang]], and three first-round draft picks.{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz Acquire Former NBA Defensive Player of the Year and Two-Time NBA All-Star Jaren Jackson Jr. {{!}} Utah Jazz |url=https://utahjazz.com/news/utah-jazz-acquire-former-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year-and-two-time-nba-all-star-jaren-jackson-jr |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=utahjazz.com |language=en}} On February 7, Jackson Jr. made his debut for the Jazz in a 120–117 loss to the [[2025–26 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]], recording 22 points, five rebounds, three assists, and two steals.{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810605 |title= Magic overcome a 17-point deficit to beat the Jazz 120-117 |publisher=ESPN|date=February 7, 2026}} He made three starts for Utah, averaging 22.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 2.7 assists.
